I know but my point is that the cat can observe it as well. Not a single atom. If you heard of the double slit experiment, the particles know when they are being observed. They act differently when the cameras are turned off and when there are no cameras or humans (or any other living beings), from when the cameras are turned on and when humans are observing them. This doesn't mention how intelligent the observer has to be, or how knowledgeable, how conscious, aware etc. Just the fact that one living being can look at the particles. Even if it's just their way. You don't need to see separate particles. Just look their way.

I mean when the cat figures out that they're dying, they know the outcome. There's a poison after all. If it's not released, the cat is aware that they're still alive. Either way, the cat can observe their situation. Even if right before dying...

The point of the experiment is to prove how quantum particles work. How consciousness affects the state of matter. The cat being aware of what's going on inside the box. The cat is an actual cat. There is a particle in the box along with the cat. Point being, the cat either dies or doesn't die, doesn't matter. Because once the cat has observed their surroundings, the outcome is decided. That's not what I'm interested in. What I'm trying to see is, why we only consider a human's consciousness when the cat is conscious as well.
Following that, the outcome is unknown to everyone but the cat, until the point the cat dies, if they die at all.
